name: Semax

lead: Semax is a seven-amino-acid peptide (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) derived from a fragment of ACTH. It originates in Russian research and is reportedly used there for stroke and other neurological conditions [1][5][11]. It is discussed on looksmax.org mainly as a focus and study aid rather than as a looks compound, and forum users disagree about whether it does anything [19][24][20].
Published work includes small, mostly Russian-language clinical studies in stroke and optic nerve disease, and many animal and cell studies [3][4][8]. No study has examined it for appearance.

paras: In rats it raises brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF) and its receptor trkB in the hippocampus after intranasal application, and it alters gene expression after experimental stroke [9][10][12]. Imaging work has examined effects on brain network connectivity [13]. Human mechanisms are less well characterized.

Long-term safety data are limited outside Russia, and reviews of therapeutic peptides note a lack of clinical trials [2]. It is not approved by the FDA or EMA [1]. Users on forums frequently buy it from unregulated sources and some are teenagers asking about use [6][7].

lead: Semax is a synthetic heptapeptide (Met-Glu-His-Phe-Pro-Gly-Pro) that combines an ACTH(4-7) fragment with a Pro-Gly-Pro tail, giving a long-lasting analogue of ACTH(4-10) without hormonal activity [1][2]. It was developed in Russia and is described in Russian literature as a nootropic and neuroprotective agent [1][3].

In published studies, it has been tested in patients with ischemic stroke, optic nerve disease and motor neuron disease [4][5][6][7], and in laboratory models of brain ischemia, where researchers report effects on neurotrophin and immune-related gene expression [8][2][9]. A 2026 review of peptides in orthopaedics describes semax among neuroactive peptides and notes the lack of clinical trials for that field [10].

Semax is not an appearance compound. It appears in looksmaxxing spaces because the communities also discuss peptides, and users talk about it as a cognitive or study aid, with views ranging from enthusiastic to dismissive [11][12][13].
infobox: Described as approved in Russia; not FDA/EMA approved [1]

paras: Stroke. A 1997 controlled clinical study of semax in 30 patients with acute hemispheric ischemic stroke compared them with 80 patients treated with conventional therapy, using clinical rating scales and electrophysiological measures [5]. A later clinical study (2018) of 110 post-stroke patients assessed plasma BDNF levels, motor performance and Barthel index scores in patients given semax or not, with early and late rehabilitation groups [4].

Other conditions. Russian-language controlled studies have examined semax in optic nerve disease and, in a randomized comparative study, in motor neuron disease [6][7]. Reviews of neuroprotective peptides in older people discuss its clinical use [14].

Healthy people and appearance. No published trials have examined semax for appearance, for focus or study performance in healthy students, or for ADHD. The statements about cognition that circulate in forums derive from animal and stroke research rather than from such trials. Reviews of therapeutic peptides describe a lack of clinical trials for many peptides, semax included [10][15].

Laboratory research. In rats, a single application raised hippocampal BDNF protein and trkB phosphorylation [2]. Studies in rat brain after experimentally induced ischemia reported changes in neurotrophin and immune-response gene expression [8][9]. Functional connectivity studies, including of the default mode network, have been reported in humans [16].

Semax was designed in Russia as a modified ACTH(4-10) fragment; a review published in 1997 described fifteen years of work on its design and study [3]. After intranasal application it has reported effects on learning in animals and neuroprotective activity [2]. Proposed mechanisms include induction of BDNF and trkB expression and changes to gene transcription after ischemia, and one review has suggested that transthyretin may mediate neuroprotective effects [8][2][17]. Review authors describe semax among peptides regarded as antistress factors in Russian stress research [18].

On looksmax.org, threads ask about semax and the related peptide selank for study performance, exam stress, ADHD and teenage use, sometimes asking for doses, sources or comparisons [19][20][11]. Replies range from describing it as ineffective to recommending prescription medication or growth hormone instead [19][11]. Other threads ask whether it makes users permanently smarter or whether such peptides are "cope" [12][13].

On T Nation, semax appears in nootropic stack discussions and in user suggestions combined with other agents, as well as in a short thread about libido effects [21][22][23]. The wiki does not reproduce preparation, dosing or sourcing details.
